doc.name: Fine Structure
doc.instructions:
Fine Structure builds and hosts complete web applications for the connected account: React pages, a managed database (called entities), authentication, publishing, custom domains with automatic TLS, restorable Saved Versions, traffic analytics, and autonomous AI agents with real messaging channels.

Agents are the part people do not expect, so offer them explicitly. An agent created with create_agent is a standing worker on the account, not a chat session: it gets its own email address, it can message its verified owner on WhatsApp and by email through the platform system channels, it can read and write the app database, and schedule_agent_task gives it recurring work (once, hourly, daily, weekly or cron, in the owner timezone). Typical uses: follow up new leads on WhatsApp every morning, watch a published app for runtime errors and report them, send a weekly summary of traffic and new records, answer inbound email.

The WhatsApp side is drivable from here, so offer it instead of sending the user to a settings screen. get_agent_whatsapp reports whether the owner phone is verified and which platform numbers are connectable. If it is not verified, ask for the owner own WhatsApp number, call start_owner_phone_verification, ask for the 6-digit code that arrives, and call confirm_owner_phone_verification. That one-time proof is what lets agents message the owner at all. Then attach_agent_whatsapp connects a platform number, and the owner can message that number from their verified phone and reach that specific agent. No WhatsApp Business account, no message template approval, nothing to buy. A number already used by another account is still a valid choice: it answers only this owner verified phone.

Messaging people other than the verified owner needs a channel the owner connects in the Fine Structure Studio, so say that plainly rather than promising it. Call get_platform_guide with sections ["agents"] for the full capability list.

Existing agents are managed from here too: get_agent and update_agent read and edit one, set_agent_status pauses, resumes or archives it, list_agent_activity shows what the agents did, list_agent_approvals shows what waits for the owner, get_credit_balance gives both balances, and update_agent_task, archive_agent_task, run_agent_task_now, stop_agent_task and cancel_agent_run control the work. Goals, triggers, org goals, memories and team templates have their own tools (list_agent_goals, create_agent_trigger, list_org_goals, list_agent_memories, create_agent_team), and list_connections and get_connection_status say which services the account has connected.

With the optional contracts, payments and members scopes: list_contract_workspaces opens the account's contracts and e-signature (read them, follow signing, prepare drafts from templates, and with contracts:send send them, remind signers or stop one; show the owner the recipients and the invitation and get a yes before send_contract), list_app_payments and get_app_payment_settings read what an app's customers paid through Cardcom, and verify_app_member and block_app_member manage the people who signed up to an app.

Knowledge: the owner's Business Brain and each app keep knowledge notebooks. list_knowledge_notebooks, add_knowledge_document and ask_knowledge_notebook read, add to and answer from them, with sources. A recording or document on the user's computer (a meeting, a call, a folder of recordings) goes in with create_knowledge_upload when you can run a command there: it returns a curl or Python command that sends the file straight to the notebook, where a recording is transcribed, within the account's transcription allowance.

First contact: when list_apps comes back empty, or the user connected this server and has not asked for anything specific, do not wait for instructions. Offer three concrete builds you can finish right now, for example a CRM with customers, jobs and invoices, a landing page with a lead form, or a booking system, and say plainly that the result will be live at a public link they can open and share. Then build the one they pick end to end without pausing for approval between steps, and hand back the live URL. A new user understands this platform through a finished app they did not have ten minutes earlier, not through a list of capabilities.

Orientation: call get_platform_guide once at the start of a working session to learn the platform conventions, and list_apps to see what the account already has. get_recommended_workflow returns the tool sequence for a given task type.

Building: create_app generates a complete app from a detailed natural-language prompt and returns a job_id; poll get_job_status until it is done, then publish_app, then share the live URL from get_app_links. For an existing app, edit files with write_app_file or patch_app_file, or stage a change set and apply it atomically. Run validate_app before publishing, and get_errors after.

Useful things to offer someone connecting for the first time: build and publish a real app such as a CRM, booking system, client portal or landing page; connect a custom domain; put a page behind login; look at runtime errors and fix them; read traffic analytics; set up an agent that runs on a schedule and reports back.

Costs: create_app, agency_create_client_app and update_app start a build that is billed like the same build in the Studio, from the account's build credits, and a build needs at least one credit left to start. Agent runs spend agent credits. Publishing, file edits, domains, data tools and analytics are free, so a small change is cheaper as a file edit than as update_app. Publish once a round of changes is validated, not after every edit: each publish replaces what live visitors see. A free tier exists.

Safety: every write creates a restorable Saved Version. Tools whose annotations mark them destructive delete or replace data, so confirm with the account owner before calling one. Authentication and credit errors are not retryable: report them to the user instead of looping. For insufficient_credits, explain the result in the user's language, and when the result carries an upgrade_url, include it as a clickable link. Retry only after the user has replenished their credits.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create a new application from a natural language prompt. The AI generates a complete web app with pages, components, styling, and data models. Returns a job_id - poll get_job_status to track progress. When the job is done, the app is ready.

prompt.description: Detailed description of the app to build

tools.title: Create App

tools.name: agency_create_client
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create or update a client record for an account-level agent. This does not create a verified Fine Structure user account and does not transfer ownership.

client_email.description: Client email that will be allowed to claim projects

note.description: Optional internal note for the agency

tools.title: Agency: Create Client

tools.name: agency_list_clients
tools.description: Agency mode only. List client records and app handoff status for the authenticated agent.

include_handoffs.description: Include claim links status without raw tokens

tools.title: Agency: List Clients

tools.name: agency_create_client_app
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create a new app owned by the agent, start generation, and create a claim link for the client. Ownership transfers only when the invited client logs in with the same email and accepts the claim link.

client_email.description: Client email allowed to claim ownership

prompt.description: Detailed description of the app to build

keep_agent_collaborator.description: After claim, invite the agent back as an editor collaborator

tools.title: Agency: Create Client App

tools.name: agency_create_claim_link
tools.description: Agency mode only. Create a client claim link for an existing app owned by the agent. The client must log in with the invited email before ownership transfers.

app_id.description: Existing app ID owned by the agent

client_email.description: Client email allowed to claim ownership

keep_agent_collaborator.description: Invite agent as editor after claim

tools.title: Agency: Create Claim Link

tools.name: agency_get_claim_status
tools.description: Agency mode only. Inspect one handoff status without exposing the raw claim token.

handoff_id.description: Handoff ID returned by agency_create_claim_link or agency_create_client_app

tools.title: Agency: Get Claim Status

tools.name: update_app
tools.description: Update an existing application with a new prompt. The AI modifies the app based on your instructions. Creates a Saved Version before the update. Returns a job_id - poll get_job_status to track progress.

prompt.description: What to change in the app

tools.title: Update App

tools.name: publish_app
tools.description: Publish an app - freeze current state and make it live at a URL. Also configures whether the public URL is open, app-login gated, private, or inferred from the app.

access_mode.description: Live access policy. public_open = anyone can view. public_auth = public URL opens but app login is required. private = published snapshot remains owner/collaborator-only. keep = preserve current visibility/auth settings. infer = choose from existing settings and obvious app structure.

auth_required.description: Optional explicit override for generated-app login requirement. Prefer access_mode when possible.

make_public.description: Optional explicit override for whether published URLs are publicly reachable. Prefer access_mode when possible.

tools.title: Publish App

tools.name: get_platform_guide
tools.description: Return a machine-readable Fine Structure / FSe2 guide for AI agents. Call this at the start of an MCP session to learn app files, entities, safe edit workflows, validation, publishing, A/B testing, secrets, and platform rules.

app_id.description: Optional app ID. If provided, the guide includes a safe app context summary.

sections.description: Optional subset of guide sections to return.

task_type.description: Optional task hint, for example edit_app, direct_file_edit, seed_data, or publish_app.

tools.title: Get Platform Guide

tools.name: get_recommended_workflow
tools.description: Return the recommended MCP tool sequence for a task type. Use this before creating apps, editing files, seeding data, publishing, setting up A/B tests, restoring versions, or configuring secrets/integrations.

goal.description: Optional short description of the user's goal.

app_id.description: Optional app ID. If provided, the workflow includes a safe app context summary.

tools.title: Get Recommended Workflow

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Poll the status of an async generation job. Use this after create_app or update_app to know when the job is done. Returns status ('running' or 'done'), progress events, and result summary when complete.

job_id.description: The job_id returned by create_app or update_app

tools.title: Get Job Status

tools.name: get_app_status
tools.description: Get app overview: files, published state, URL, active jobs.
tools.title: Get App Status

tools.name: get_app_links
tools.description: Return editor, preview, published path, subdomain, and custom-domain links plus whether each works for anonymous visitors, app users, or Studio users based on publish and auth settings.
tools.title: Get App Links

tools.name: list_app_domains
tools.description: List an app's platform path, subdomain, and configured custom domain with verification, SSL, primary-domain, redirect, publish, and login-gating status.
tools.title: List App Domains

tools.name: set_app_subdomain
tools.description: Set or clear the app platform subdomain - the '<subdomain>.<base domain>' host Fine Structure already serves the app on. Runs the same ownership, format, reserved-name and uniqueness checks as the Studio subdomain field because it calls the same model function. Replacing a subdomain takes effect immediately and creates NO redirect: the previous name stops resolving to this app and is released for anyone to claim. Pass an empty subdomain to clear it. For a domain the user owns, use add_custom_domain instead.

subdomain.description: Subdomain label: 3-32 characters, lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen, not a reserved platform name. Empty string clears the subdomain.

tools.title: Set App Subdomain

tools.name: check_subdomain_available
tools.description: Check whether a platform subdomain can be claimed before calling set_app_subdomain. Returns available plus a status of available, invalid, reserved, taken, current, or empty, with the exact reason. Pass app_id (an app you own) to have that app's own current subdomain reported as 'current' instead of 'taken'.

app_id.description: Optional ID of an app you own. When supplied, this app's own subdomain reports as 'current' instead of 'taken'.

tools.title: Check Subdomain Available

tools.name: add_custom_domain
tools.description: Attach or replace the app custom domain through the same Fine Structure Studio custom-domain flow. Returns exact DNS verification and routing records for the user to configure at their DNS provider.

domain.description: Custom domain to connect, for example example.com or app.example.com

tools.title: Add Custom Domain

tools.name: get_domain_verification
tools.description: Return the exact DNS records and instructions required to verify and route the app custom domain.

domain.description: Optional configured custom domain. If omitted, uses the app's current custom domain.

tools.title: Get Domain Verification

tools.name: check_domain_verification
tools.description: Check Fine Structure custom-domain verification and SSL status for the configured custom domain, then save the latest status.

domain.description: Optional configured custom domain. If omitted, uses the app's current custom domain.

tools.title: Check Domain Verification

tools.name: set_primary_domain
tools.description: Set which app host should be treated as primary for generated links and custom-domain redirects.

domain.description: Primary host, for example example.com, www.example.com, or the app subdomain host.

tools.title: Set Primary Domain

tools.name: remove_custom_domain
tools.description: Remove the configured custom domain from the app and clean up the platform-side hostname registration when possible.

domain.description: Optional configured custom domain. If omitted, removes the current custom domain.

tools.title: Remove Custom Domain

tools.name: get_domain_ssl_status
tools.description: Return SSL/certificate status and pending certificate validation DNS records for the app custom domain.

domain.description: Optional configured custom domain. If omitted, uses the app's current custom domain.

tools.title: Get Domain SSL Status

tools.name: configure_domain_redirects
tools.description: Configure custom-domain redirect policy: primary domain, optional www/root redirect, and HTTPS enforcement.

primary_domain.description: Canonical primary domain, for example example.com

redirect_www.description: Redirect the www/root counterpart to primary_domain

force_https.description: Redirect HTTP custom-domain requests to HTTPS

tools.title: Configure Domain Redirects

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List owned and accepted Studio-shared applications, newest activity first. Returns up to `limit` apps per call plus the total count; page with `offset` when the account has more. Accepted editors can edit shared source; viewers can read it. Publishing, records, domains and security administration remain owner-only.
tools.title: List Apps

tools.name: get_app_files
tools.description: Get the file tree for an app with paths and byte sizes.
tools.title: Get App Files

tools.name: read_app_file
tools.description: Read one source file from an app's virtual filesystem. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

path.description: Virtual file path, for example pages/Home.jsx

tools.title: Read App File

tools.name: read_app_files
tools.description: Read several source files from an app's virtual filesystem. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.
tools.title: Read App Files

tools.name: write_app_file
tools.description: Create or replace one file in an app's virtual filesystem. Creates a Saved Version before changing content. Paths and file model follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.
tools.title: Write App File

tools.name: patch_app_file
tools.description: Patch one file by replacing exact text. Safer than full overwrite for targeted edits. Creates a Saved Version before changing content. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches instead of the first match

tools.title: Patch App File

tools.name: rename_app_file
tools.description: Rename or move one app source file atomically. Internally stages an upsert at new_path and a delete at old_path, validates the resulting app state, and creates a Saved Version before applying.

old_path.description: Existing virtual file path to rename

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing file at new_path

force.description: Apply even if validation reports blocking errors

tools.title: Rename App File

tools.name: get_app_detail
tools.description: Deep introspection of an app: entities, pages, settings, integrations, environment variables, and file structure. Use this to understand what an app contains before updating it.
tools.title: Get App Detail

tools.name: get_entities
tools.description: Get all entity (data model) schemas for an app, with record counts. Each entity has fields, types, and relationships.
tools.title: Get Entities

tools.name: query_entity
tools.description: Query app data records for one entity with optional exact-match filters.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix with - for descending

tools.title: Query Entity

tools.name: seed_entity
tools.description: Compatibility tool for starter-record creation. Inserts directly for the authenticated app owner; by default it only seeds an empty entity (skip_if_not_empty).

mode.description: append always inserts; skip_if_not_empty inserts only when the entity is empty

reason.description: Why these records should be created

tools.title: Seed Entity Records

tools.name: create_entity_records
tools.description: Create/insert records in one app entity. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner and returns the created record ids.

reason.description: Why these records should be created

expected_count.description: Optional safety check; the write aborts if the record count differs

tools.title: Create Entity Records

tools.name: update_entity_record
tools.description: Compatibility tool that updates one record by ID. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner.

data.description: Fields to merge into the record

reason.description: Why this record should be updated

tools.title: Update Entity Record

tools.name: update_entity_records
tools.description: Update exact records. Select explicit record_ids or exact-match filters and provide shared changes, or provide per-record updates. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner; expected_count aborts the write on a mismatch.

filters.description: One exact-match selector or a list of exact-match selectors

changes.description: Shared fields to merge into every selected record

updates.description: Per-record changes; use instead of shared changes

reason.description: Why these records should be updated

expected_count.description: Required match count safety check, when known

tools.title: Update Entity Records

tools.name: delete_entity_records
tools.description: Delete exact records by ID or exact-match filters. Executes directly for the authenticated app owner; pass expected_count as a safety check to abort on a mismatch.

filters.description: One exact-match selector or a list of exact-match selectors

reason.description: Why these records should be deleted

expected_count.description: Required match count safety check, when known

tools.title: Delete Entity Records

tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Get all pages in an app with their file paths and sizes.
tools.title: Get Pages

tools.name: get_errors
tools.description: Get recent runtime errors for an app (last 20). Useful for diagnosing issues before updating.
tools.title: Get Errors

tools.name: get_app_analytics
tools.description: Traffic analytics for an app's published site over a chosen window: total views, unique visitors, daily series, top pages, top referrer domains and device split.
tools.title: Get App Analytics

tools.name: get_preview_url
tools.description: Return editor preview and published/public URLs for an app.
tools.title: Get Preview URL

tools.name: list_saved_versions
tools.description: List restorable Saved Versions for an app, including versions created by MCP writes.
tools.title: List Saved Versions

tools.name: create_change_set
tools.description: Create a staged file change set. Add multiple file changes, validate them as one app state, then apply atomically.
tools.title: Create Change Set

tools.name: add_file_change
tools.description: Stage one file upsert or delete inside a change set. Does not modify the live app until apply_change_set. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.
tools.title: Add File Change

tools.name: validate_change_set
tools.description: Validate current app files plus staged change set files before applying.
tools.title: Validate Change Set

tools.name: apply_change_set
tools.description: Apply a staged change set to the app. Creates a Saved Version before applying. Blocks on validation errors unless force=true.

force.description: Apply even if validation has errors

tools.title: Apply Change Set

tools.name: discard_change_set
tools.description: Discard a pending staged change set without changing app files.
tools.title: Discard Change Set

tools.name: validate_app
tools.description: Run deterministic app checks: syntax, imports, routes/pages, entity schemas, missing entities, and recorded runtime errors.
tools.title: Validate App

tools.name: inspect_preview
tools.description: Return server-side preview context: URLs, persisted runtime/network errors, static clickable candidates, pages, and explicit live-browser availability.

auth_as_role.description: Optional app role simulation, e.g. staff/admin/customer

tools.title: Inspect Live Preview

tools.name: get_app_security_context
tools.description: Return safe security context for one owned app: owner id/email, Studio collaborators, generated-app members, route policies, entity policies, function policies, and recent security audit entries. Does not return secrets and does not grant access to other apps.
tools.title: Get App Security Context

tools.name: set_route_policy
tools.description: Create or update a server-owned route policy for a generated app route.
tools.title: Set Route Policy

tools.name: set_function_policy
tools.description: Create or update the server-owned access policy of a backend function (functions/<name>.js). Without a policy a function answers only to the app owner's Studio token (401 for app visitors and webhooks). Recipes: anonymous checkout step or inbound webhook/IPN -> require_auth=false; signed-in members -> require_auth=true + allowed_roles (e.g. ['authenticated'] or ['admin','staff']); webhook with a shared secret -> require_secret=true + secret_name (an app secret) that the caller sends in secret_header. allowed_hosts fences the function's outbound network to those hosts plus the platform backend; omit it for open egress.

require_auth.description: false = anonymous visitors and external callers may invoke

allowed_roles.description: App roles allowed when require_auth is true; 'authenticated' = any signed-in app member

require_secret.description: Caller must send a shared secret header (webhooks)

secret_name.description: Name of the app secret holding the shared value (set_secret)

secret_header.description: Header the caller sends the shared secret in

allowed_hosts.description: Outbound egress allow-list of host[:port] entries, e.g. ['api.takbull.co.il']. Omit to keep the stored list; pass [] to open egress again

sdk_identity.description: Whose identity the SDK inside the function uses. 'caller' (default): the function reads data as whoever called it, so an anonymous call sees only what anonymous may read. 'app': the SDK acts as the app owner on THIS app's entities (a checkout or payment IPN that must load/update orders whose read policy is owner/admin/staff); the caller still counts as anonymous for rate limits, audit and X-FSe2-Caller-Type. Owner-only. Omit to keep the stored value

tools.title: Set Function Policy

tools.name: invoke_function
tools.description: Run a backend function of an owned app exactly like the HTTP route and return its status and JSON. caller='owner' runs as the app owner; caller='anonymous' first evaluates the function policy as a public visitor and returns the 401/403 decision without running when access would be denied. Use it to verify a function (secrets, outbound calls, policy) before wiring it into the app.

params.description: JSON body passed to the function

headers.description: Optional extra request headers to simulate, e.g. a webhook secret header

tools.title: Invoke Function

tools.name: create_platform_request
tools.description: Open a request to the Fine Structure platform team: a bug, a feature request or a question about the platform itself (not about the user's app). Use it when something in the platform blocks you instead of working around it. Give a reproduction the team can run (invoke_function / curl / the exact tool call and result), what you expected, and how the team will know it is closed. Credential-looking values are redacted. Returns request_id and a Studio URL; the team's replies, status changes and deployments come back through get_platform_request / list_platform_requests. Limits: 20 per account per day, 32 KB.

title.description: One line, what is wrong or missing

body.description: Free text, markdown allowed: context, impact, what you tried

app_id.description: Optional: the app where it showed up

reproduction.description: Steps, invoke_function calls or curl commands that reproduce it

acceptance.description: How the team will know it is closed

attachments.description: Optional app file paths or log ids

tools.title: Create Platform Request

tools.name: get_platform_request
tools.description: One platform request with its full history: team replies, status changes (open | triaged | in_progress | needs_info | deployed | wont_fix) and what was deployed (commit, time). Pass since=<ISO timestamp> to get only the events after it.

since.description: Optional ISO timestamp: only events after it

tools.title: Get Platform Request

tools.name: list_platform_requests
tools.description: Your account's platform requests, newest activity first. Call it at the start of a session with since=<the updated_date you last saw> to learn what changed: replies, needs_info questions to answer, deployments with their commit. Filters: app_id, status.

since.description: Optional ISO timestamp: only requests touched after it, each with changes_since

tools.title: List Platform Requests

tools.name: reply_platform_request
tools.description: Add a reply or a finding to one of your platform requests without opening a new one, e.g. to answer a needs_info question (that reopens it).

body.description: The answer or finding (markdown allowed, credentials are redacted)

as_team.description: Platform team only: reply as the team (mails the requester)

tools.title: Reply Platform Request

tools.name: update_platform_request
tools.description: Platform team only: set the status of a request (open | triaged | in_progress | needs_info | deployed | wont_fix), attach the deployed commit and/or reply. deployed and needs_info mail the requester.

deployed_commit.description: Commit hash or tag that shipped it

tools.title: Update Platform Request

tools.name: set_entity_policy
tools.description: Replace server-side entity access policy. Optional action rules override read/write roles and can allow public create without public read, update, or delete. Omitting rules replaces any existing action rules with read/write role behavior.

read.description: Roles allowed to read when rules are omitted

write.description: Roles allowed to write when rules are omitted

rules.description: Nonempty unconditional action/role rules. No matching rule denies access. Include owner/admin actions explicitly. Record conditions are not supported by this MCP input.

tools.title: Set Entity Policy

tools.name: list_app_members
tools.description: List generated-app runtime users/members for an app. This is separate from Studio project collaborators.
tools.title: List App Members

tools.name: invite_app_member
tools.description: Provision a generated-app runtime member with a role. This does not create a Studio collaborator, and the owner role cannot be assigned. password is required: ask the account owner which password the member should get. This tool never generates one, because a generated password would come back in the result and that is a live credential in the conversation transcript.

password.description: The password this member signs in with, chosen by the account owner. Required, and never echoed back in the result.

tools.title: Invite App Member

tools.name: update_app_member_role
tools.description: Update a generated-app runtime member role. This cannot assign owner and cannot change the Fine Structure account owner.
tools.title: Update App Member Role

tools.name: remove_app_member
tools.description: Remove a person's access to the app. They are blocked, as with block_app_member: their sessions end and the address can neither sign in nor sign up again. Nothing is deleted, and unblock_app_member gives the access back.
tools.title: Remove App Member

tools.name: get_app_security_audit
tools.description: Read recent server-side security audit events for an app.
tools.title: Get App Security Audit

tools.name: compare_saved_versions
tools.description: Compare two Saved Versions and return per-file additions, removals, modifications, and compact diffs.
tools.title: Compare Saved Versions

tools.name: compare_current_to_version
tools.description: Compare the current app files to a Saved Version and return compact per-file diffs.
tools.title: Compare Current To Version

tools.name: restore_file_from_version
tools.description: Restore one file from a Saved Version instead of restoring the entire app. Creates a Saved Version before changing the file. Paths follow the Fine Structure app file API, documented at https://finestructure.ai/api/mcp/docs.
tools.title: Restore File From Version

tools.name: create_entity_schema
tools.description: Create an entity schema file in entities/<Entity>.json. Creates a Saved Version before writing.
tools.title: Create Entity Schema

tools.name: update_entity_schema
tools.description: Replace or shallow-merge an existing entity schema file. Creates a Saved Version before writing.

schema.description: Schema fields to set or merge

tools.title: Update Entity Schema

tools.name: validate_entity_relationships
tools.description: Validate entity relationship metadata and *_id references against existing entity schemas.
tools.title: Validate Entity Relationships

tools.name: update_entity_metadata
tools.description: Set relationship/index metadata on an entity schema. This stores metadata in the schema file; DB index creation is automatic where supported by the platform.
tools.title: Update Entity Metadata

tools.name: list_secret_keys
tools.description: List secret key names for an app. Secret values are never returned.
tools.title: List Secret Keys

tools.name: set_secret
tools.description: Create or update one encrypted app secret. The secret value is never returned.

value.description: Secret value to encrypt and store

tools.title: Set Secret

tools.name: delete_secret
tools.description: Delete one app secret by key.
tools.title: Delete Secret

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: List supported integrations and safe connected integration metadata for an app. Tokens/secrets are never returned.
tools.title: List Integrations

tools.name: configure_integration
tools.description: Store safe non-secret integration metadata for an app. Use set_secret for API keys/tokens.

config.description: Safe metadata only, such as workspace/team/name/email

is_active.description: Set false to disconnect this integration metadata

tools.title: Configure Integration

tools.name: list_ab_tests
tools.description: List the platform A/B tests configured for an app.
tools.title: List A/B Tests

tools.name: create_ab_test
tools.description: Create a native Fine Structure A/B test between existing app pages. Use update_app first if a variant page still needs to be generated. Creates a Saved Version before the change.

page_name.description: Base route page that triggers the experiment
Existing app page name or path

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create an autonomous AI agent on the user's Fine Structure account: a standing worker, not a chat session. It gets the platform's default safe tool policy and its own email address, it can read and write the app database, and once the owner phone is verified (see get_agent_whatsapp) it can message its owner on WhatsApp and by email through the platform system channels. Pair it with schedule_agent_task for recurring work such as following up new leads on WhatsApp each morning, watching an app for runtime errors, or sending a weekly summary. Messaging anyone other than the verified owner requires a channel the owner connects in the Fine Structure Studio.

name.description: Agent display name (e.g. 'Lead Follow-up'). Auto-derived from role when omitted.

description.description: What this agent is responsible for, one or two sentences

persona.description: Optional working style and tone instructions for the agent

app_id.description: Optional app to attach the agent to; account-level when omitted

tools.title: Create Agent

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the AI agents on the user's account with id, name, role, status and FineMail address.
tools.title: List Agents

tools.name: schedule_agent_task
tools.description: Create a scheduled task for one of the user's agents. Supported schedule types: once (run_at ISO local time + timezone), interval (interval_minutes 5-1440), hourly, daily (time HH:MM + timezone), weekly (time + timezone + days_of_week 0=Sunday..6), cron (5-field expression + timezone), manual (only runs on demand). Returns the normalized schedule and the computed next_run_at so you can read the fire time back to the user in their timezone. For 'tell me when a new X comes in' (a lead, an order, a signup, any record of an app entity) do not poll with a plain interval: set watch, and the task costs nothing until a new record arrives.

agent_id.description: The agent id (from create_agent or list_agents)

instructions.description: What the agent should do on each run, written as instructions to the agent

max_runs.description: Optional cap on total runs (0 = unlimited)

activate.description: Start the schedule immediately (true) or save as draft (false)

watch.description: Run the task only when a record is new, e.g. {"provider":"app_records","app_id":"<app id>","entity":"Lead"} with an interval schedule. The platform checks each interval with no model call and no credits, and starts the agent only when a record arrived, with those records in hand. Works for any entity of the user's own apps. Optional: where (exact field values such as {"status":"new"}), include_existing (also act on the records already there).

tools.title: Schedule Agent Task

tools.name: list_agent_tasks
tools.description: List scheduled tasks for one agent (or the whole account), including schedule, status and next_run_at.

status.description: Optional status filter: draft, active, paused, archived

tools.title: List Agent Tasks

tools.name: get_agent_whatsapp

Call this first whenever the user asks to talk to an agent on WhatsApp, and repeat its next_step to them.

agent_id.description: Optional: report only this agent's WhatsApp state.

tools.title: Get Agent Whatsapp

tools.name: start_owner_phone_verification
tools.description: Send a 6-digit code over WhatsApp to the ACCOUNT OWNER's own phone. This is the one-time ownership proof required before a platform number can be connected, and it also unlocks agents messaging the owner. Ask the user for their own WhatsApp number first and send only to that. No WhatsApp Business account is involved.

phone.description: The owner's own WhatsApp number, ideally in E.164 form such as +972501234567.

region.description: Optional ISO region hint (for example IL, US) used when the number has no country code.

tools.title: Start Owner Phone Verification

tools.name: confirm_owner_phone_verification
tools.description: Confirm the 6-digit code the owner received on WhatsApp from start_owner_phone_verification. On success the owner is verified: agents can message them, and platform numbers become connectable.

phone.description: The same phone number the code was sent to.

code.description: The 6-digit code from the WhatsApp message.

region.description: Optional ISO region hint, matching the one used when sending.

tools.title: Confirm Owner Phone Verification

tools.name: attach_agent_whatsapp
tools.description: Connect a platform WhatsApp number to one of the account's agents, so the owner can message that number and reach that agent. Requires the owner to be verified first. Take phone_number_id from get_agent_whatsapp. A number already used by another account is still valid to connect: it answers only this owner's verified phone.

agent_id.description: The agent that should answer on this number.

tools.title: Attach Agent Whatsapp

tools.name: detach_agent_whatsapp
tools.description: Disconnect the owner's WhatsApp route from a platform number. Removes only this account's route; other accounts sharing the number keep theirs.

tools.name: send_agent_message

Returns acceptance and a durable task_id immediately, NOT a completed answer. Poll get_agent_task and read get_agent_conversation for the actual response. Work continues after MCP disconnects. A follow-up in a busy conversation uses the normal queue. Customer conversations are readable but cannot be impersonated by this tool.

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID returned by these tools.

tools.title: Send Agent Message

tools.name: get_agent_conversation

A recording takes one place in the account's transcription allowance, which depends on its plan and renews with its credits; the reply says how many places are left. filename.description: The file's name with its extension, e.g. meeting-11-12.m4a.

size_bytes.description: The exact file size in bytes.

sha256.description: Optional hex sha256 of the file; a mismatch is refused.

tools.title: Retry Knowledge Document

tools.name: ask_knowledge_notebook
tools.description: Ask a notebook a question; the answer comes from its documents, with sources. Waits up to 25 seconds for the answer, otherwise returns the query_job_id for get_knowledge_answer. Without chat_session_id a new conversation starts.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

source_ids.description: Optional: answer only from these documents.

tools.title: Ask Knowledge Notebook

tools.name: set_knowledge_webhook_enabled
tools.description: Turn an ingest webhook off (posts are refused) or on again.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

tools.title: Set Knowledge Webhook Enabled

tools.name: scan_knowledge_for_sensitive_data
tools.description: Scan documents for personal or sensitive information, or for what the owner's instructions describe. Only finds; nothing changes until apply_knowledge_redaction. Runs in the background; read it with get_knowledge_redaction_run.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

instructions.description: Optional: what to find, in the owner's words.

tools.title: Scan Knowledge For Sensitive Data

tools.name: apply_knowledge_redaction
tools.description: Redact the chosen findings of a scan: approved maps each document id to the finding ids to replace. The original text is kept, so revert_knowledge_redaction can undo it.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

tools.title: Apply Knowledge Redaction

tools.name: revert_knowledge_redaction
tools.description: Undo an applied redaction: the documents get their original text back.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

tools.title: Revert Knowledge Redaction

tools.name: set_knowledge_redaction_policy
tools.description: Set a notebook's automatic redaction for new uploads: on or off, what to find (instructions), whether findings above min_confidence are applied at once. Originals are always kept.

app_id.description: Optional app whose notebooks to use. Omitted: the owner's own Business Brain.

tools.title: Set Knowledge Redaction Policy

tools.name: list_whatsapp_triggers
tools.description: The app's WhatsApp triggers: the message sent to a customer when a record is created, the page and entity, the phone field, the sending number and whether it is on.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

tools.title: List Whatsapp Triggers

tools.name: get_whatsapp_trigger_options
tools.description: What a WhatsApp trigger can use in this app: the owner's WhatsApp numbers and flows, and the pages, entities and fields that create records.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

tools.title: Get Whatsapp Trigger Options

tools.name: list_whatsapp_trigger_logs
tools.description: What the app's WhatsApp triggers sent, newest first, with the outcome of each send.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

tools.title: List Whatsapp Trigger Logs

tools.name: create_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Save a WhatsApp trigger for record-created events. It is saved switched off and messages no one. Switching it on is done by the owner on the app's Automations screen in Fine Structure.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

page_name.description: The page whose form creates the record.

entity_name.description: The entity whose new records fire it.

phone_field.description: The record field holding the customer's WhatsApp number.

message_template.description: The message; {{ field_name }} inserts a record field.

whatsapp_bot_id.description: The WhatsApp number that sends, from get_whatsapp_trigger_options.

flow_id.description: Optional WhatsApp flow the conversation continues in.

tools.title: Create Whatsapp Trigger

tools.name: update_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Change a trigger that is switched off: page, entity, fields, message, number or flow. Only the fields given change. A trigger that is on is turned off first with disable_whatsapp_trigger.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

page_name.description: The page whose form creates the record.

entity_name.description: The entity whose new records fire it.

phone_field.description: The record field holding the customer's WhatsApp number.

message_template.description: The message; {{ field_name }} inserts a record field.

whatsapp_bot_id.description: The WhatsApp number that sends, from get_whatsapp_trigger_options.

flow_id.description: Optional WhatsApp flow the conversation continues in.

tools.title: Update Whatsapp Trigger

tools.name: disable_whatsapp_trigger
tools.description: Switch a WhatsApp trigger off: new records no longer send its message. It stays saved.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

tools.title: Disable Whatsapp Trigger

tools.name: send_whatsapp_trigger_test
tools.description: Send a saved trigger's message once to the owner's own verified WhatsApp number, rendered with a sample record, from the trigger's sending number. It never goes to anyone else.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

sample_record.description: Field values to render the message with.

tools.title: Send Whatsapp Trigger Test

tools.name: suggest_whatsapp_trigger_message
tools.description: Have the AI write a WhatsApp message for a trigger from the page it follows, the app's brain and the record fields. Returns text to review; nothing is saved or sent.

app_id.description: The app the trigger belongs to.

tools.title: Suggest Whatsapp Trigger Message
